As a Cavs fan, it worries me. Because LeBron is truly the best player in the world right now, and this team would be lost without him. That being said, I think having a great coach is invaluable. I think the best teams have tenured coaches that have built a system. Look at the NBA champions in the last decade. Spurs, Heat, Celtics, Lakers, etc. When they won their titles, they had a respected coach.

Players come and go. Bron could get injured tomorrow and never play again. Bron will slow down and be less impactful and eventually retire over the next 10 years. A coach/front office can last way longer. The Heat, despite losing the best player in the world, still remained competitive and actually almost made the playoffs, because they have a strong culture and coach, backed up by the front office.

As a Cavs fan and not a LeBron fan, I want to build a culture. I think Blatt is incredible. He's new to the NBA, but he's had years of success. He knows what he's doing. He's intelligent. He's great. He doesn't know what's best for this franchise.
